note: Real partial mutation evidence. The conformance test at crates/tooling/chio-conformance/tests/threats/kernel_impersonation.rs calls chio_kernel_core::sign_receipt_relaying_trusted_body with a receipt body claiming the legitimate kernel key and a same-algorithm attacker signing backend, then requires ReceiptSigningError::KernelKeyMismatch. It separately proves that replacing the embedded kernel_key after signing makes ChioReceipt::verify_signature return false, and retains a genuine-receipt positive control. A targeted cargo-mutants run replaced the production signer's algorithm-mismatch OR key-mismatch guard with AND; the same-algorithm attacker key bypassed the weakened guard and the conformance test caught the mutant. PARTIAL: authenticated service identity, verifier trust-anchor distribution, and rotation discipline remain deployment follow-up.
